answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a continuous chain of sequential modular squarings before it can participate. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the result efficiently, while the dependency between squarings prevents GPUs from shortening the delay for any one chain. An attacker may run clones in parallel, but must pay the sequential time cost for each; atlas, raven, and kernel are labels, not shortcuts around that bottleneck.
